'''''Cenchrus echinatus''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known by the common names '''southern sandbur''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=CEEC|taxon=Cenchrus echinatus|accessdate=13 January 2016}}</ref> '''spiny sandbur''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''southern sandspur''', and in Australia, '''Mossman River grass'''.<ref>{{cite web|title = University of Florida IFAS Extension Southern Sandspur (Southern Sandbur), ''Cenchrus echinatus'' L.|url = http://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/fw009|access-date = 2008-06-15|archive-date = 2008-06-20|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080620062849/http://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/FW009}}</ref><ref name=au>[http://www.weeds.org.au/cgi-bin/weedident.cgi?tpl=plant.tpl&state=&s=&ibra=all&card=G10 ''Cenchrus echinatus''.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090918083205/http://www.weeds.org.au/cgi-bin/weedident.cgi?tpl=plant.tpl&state=&s=&ibra=all&card=G10 |date=September 18, 2009 }} National Weeds Strategy.</ref> It is native to North and South America.
It is a clump-forming annual grass growing up to {{Convert|80|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall. The leaves occur with or without hairs and measure up to {{Convert|12|mm|in|abbr=on}} wide. The ligule is a fringe of hairs. The grass has barbed burrs of {{Convert|4|-|10|mm|abbr=on}} long.

In Australia it forms an invasive weed in coastal situations.<ref name=au/>

==Ecology==
The species is invasive in [[New Caledonia]],<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://horizon.documentation.ird.fr/exl-doc/pleins_textes/divers12-08/010052239.pdf|title=LES ESPÈCES EXOTIQUES ENVAHISSANTES DE NOUVELLE-CALÉDONIE|last=Hequet|first=Vanessa|year=2009|page=17|language=fr}}</ref> [[Tahiti]], and [[Rarotonga]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Piri-Piri ~ Piripiri|work=Te Māra Reo: The Language Garden|year=2022|publisher=Benton Family Trust|url=https://www.temarareo.org/PPN-Piripiri.html|access-date=29 November 2022}}</ref>
